title: Tea workers vote in first union election in eight years
excerpt: Bangladesh Cha Sramik Union members vote today at 230 tea gardens in five districts, its first election since 2018, bdnews24 and Bonik Barta report.
content:
MOULVIBAZAR, 28 November 2026: Tea workers in 230 gardens across five districts are voting today, Saturday (28 November), to elect the leaders of the Bangladesh Cha Sramik Union (Bangladesh Tea Workers' Union), its first election in eight years, bdnews24.com reported on Friday (27 November) and Bonik Barta reported on Saturday.

Voting runs from 8am to 4pm in 20 upazilas of Moulvibazar, Sylhet, Habiganj, Chattogram and Rangamati, according to the Department of Labour, which is running the election. Each garden is one polling centre. Only union members who pay the monthly subscription of Tk 15 can vote. Both outlets put the electorate at more than 100,000. Moulvibazar has the most, with 135 gardens and about 60,500 voters (bdnews24 gave 60,492, Bonik Barta 60,482). Tea workers in Panchagarh are not union members and are not voting.

The last election was held on 24 June 2018. The union's constitution requires a vote every three years, but the 2021 and 2024 elections did not take place because of legal complications, including a High Court case, Bonik Barta reported.

Each voter casts three ballots: one for the 30-member central committee, one for their valley committee and one for the panchayat committee of the garden where they work and live. The central committee includes a reserved post of women's vice-president and a women's secretary. Pankaj Kanda of Lakhaichhara garden in Sreemangal and Raju Goala of Lakkatura garden in Sylhet are standing for president. Paresh Kalindi, Nipen Pal and Mukesh Karmakar are standing for general secretary. Election officials told bdnews24 that about 7,000 candidates are standing on more than 600 panels.

Sreemangal Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Ziaur Rahman told bdnews24 that the government gave a Tk 50 lakh grant for the election and the union paid Tk 25 lakh, taken from workers' subscriptions. "Those elected will serve for three years. They will work to protect workers' interests through discussions and agreements with the owners," he said.

Why it matters

The union leaders elected today will negotiate and sign agreements with garden owners on behalf of more than 100,000 members, after years in which the leadership had no fresh mandate. Panchayat committees also settle family and local disputes in the gardens, bdnews24 noted, though they are no substitute for the courts. For NGOs working on labour rights, legal aid, health and education in tea communities, the new leadership will be a key partner. Devlens has followed wage bargaining in the garment sector, where the wage board set a Tk 17,000 minimum this week after tense talks.

What to watch

  • Counting after polls close at 4pm, and whether any results are disputed.
  • How many women win panchayat and valley seats, beyond the reserved central posts.
  • The new committee's first talks with garden owners on wages and benefits.

Sources
